items.followUp: How does active transport differ from diffusion?

rubric.why: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient, from low to high concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that substances move against the concentration gradient or from low to high concentration.

rubric.why: Active transport requires energy, usually supplied by ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning energy or ATP.

modelAnswer: Active transport is the movement of substances across a cell membrane from low concentration to high concentration, against their concentration gradient.
This movement requires energy, usually supplied by ATP.

items.followUp: What happens to a plant cell when it is placed in a hypertonic solution?

rubric.why: Water loss from the plant cell leads to plasmolysis.
rubric.description: States that the cell loses water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing water loss or outward movement of water.

rubric.why: During plasmolysis, the protoplast shrinks and pulls away from the cell wall.
rubric.description: Describes the shrinkage away from the cell wall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the protoplast or cytoplasm shrinks or pulls away from the cell wall.

modelAnswer: Plasmolysis is the shrinkage of the protoplast when a plant cell loses water in a hypertonic solution.
The protoplast shrinks away from the cell wall.
